talking_points.headline: HSBC opens CFO succession search after Pam Kaur sets 2027 exit
talking_points.context_html: Pam Kaur, HSBC Group Chief Financial Officer, will step down in 2027 and move into an advisory role to the Group CEO, ending a landmark tenure as the first woman to hold the post. The board's search — spanning internal and external candidates — lands just as HSBC works through a 33% H1 profit rebound and the German transaction-services wind-down, so whoever inherits the CFO seat also inherits sponsorship of the cost and restructuring agenda your change programmes run through.
source_links: Who HSBC may tap as next CFO

talking_points.headline: Citi keeps poaching: $3bn adviser hired from Bank of America for UHNW push
talking_points.context_html: Teresa Radzinski, who managed roughly $3 billion in assets at Bank of America Private Bank, has joined Citi's team serving clients above $500 million net worth — days after Citi Wealth hired Liz McElherne to lead its alternatives platform. Both hires sit inside Andy Sieg, Head of Citi Wealth's plan to add roughly 500 advisers and 100 private bankers. The pattern — buying UHNW and alternatives coverage banker-by-banker rather than building it — is the same RM-poaching pressure bearing on HSBC Private Bank's own family-office and UHNW franchise.

HSBC News.title: HSBC Launches CFO Succession Search as Pam Kaur Sets 2027 Departure
HSBC News.summary: HSBC has begun searching for a new Group CFO after Pam Kaur, the first woman to hold the role, announced she will step down in 2027 and move into an advisory post to the Group CEO. The board is weighing internal and external candidates as the bank continues restructuring under a 33% H1 profit rebound.

Competitor Intelligence.title: Citi Private Bank Hires $3bn Adviser Teresa Radzinski From Bank of America
Competitor Intelligence.summary: Citi Private Bank has hired Teresa Radzinski, who managed around $3 billion in client assets at Bank of America Private Bank, to serve ultra-high-net-worth clients above $500 million from Jacksonville, Florida. The hire follows Citi Wealth's addition of an alternatives platform chief days earlier as part of a push to add roughly 500 advisers.
